title: FUNDING-INVENTORY-2026-11-06 (1)
universal_lens: The funding inventory defines a discrete-time, multi-state Markov process over a finite set of capital acquisition channels. The system evolves via stochastic state transitions (Drafted -> Submitted -> Approved/Blocked), governed by time-dependent decay functions representing credit expiration and decision windows.
gsi_mapping: GSI models the pipeline as a hierarchical Bayesian network where observed submission events update posterior probabilities of capital realization. Conformal prediction intervals bound the aggregate face-value exposure, accounting for censoring in pending decisions and zero-dollar non-monetary program inclusions.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the inventory as a dynamic resource allocation graph. State-transition rules dictate operational readiness based on live credits, while blocked or held nodes represent topological bottlenecks requiring explicit founder intervention to unlock future computational capacity.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if implicit valuation heuristics are applied to unpriced tiers, violating the strict exclusion rule.

layer2.telemetry: Count of excluded high-value non-monetary programs.

reasoning_traces.think:
The funding inventory operates as a constrained optimization problem over a directed acyclic graph of application states. We define the system state vector \mathbf{S} comprising disjoint sets of programs categorized by their lifecycle phase (Drafted, Submitted, Approved, Blocked). The primary observable is the aggregate face value V_{agg}, calculated as the sum of individual program maximums V_i, subject to a strict exclusion filter I_{USD} that zeroes out non-monetized tiers like NVIDIA Inception. This creates a dual-layer representation: a scalar financial projection and a topological map of operational dependencies. Transitions between states are governed by external stochastic processes (reviewer decisions) and internal deterministic triggers (founder taps for BLOCKED items). The temporal dimension introduces a decay operator D(t), where approved credits V_i(t) drop to zero upon reaching T_exp. The epistemic uncertainty lies primarily in the SUBMITTED bucket, modeled as a latent variable with a probability distribution over future states. By isolating the BLOCKED and HELD states, we identify structural bottlenecks where human agency directly dictates system evolution, decoupling them from passive waiting periods. This formalization allows us to treat the funding hunt not as a static list, but as a dynamic resource flow network with explicit failure modes and expiration singularities.
